candidates.statement: Fix a cutoff q (models with unique fillers above q). Prove 'J_n-expansions are weak equivalences' for n = q, q-1, ..., 0. At index n, build coglobular objects P_j: P_j = D_j for j<n (stationary), P_n = D_{n+1} (one joining cell), and for n<j<=q a small-object completion of the two-sided boundary datum against upper I_k. Their contractibility (and that of P(S)) follows from the already-proved higher-index expansions via whiskered shapes and skeletal gluing. Contractibility lets every coherator operation be interpreted on Hom(P_j, Y) in the free order, giving a partial path functor whose endpoints lift I_j and jointly lift J_n; a retract argument closes the step.

Here the cylinders depend on the fixed cutoff and expansion index'; 00 intro: 'His construction leaves the extension to compatible interpretations of all higher operations open. The partial paths used here are adapted to one expansion index at a time: the already established higher-index expansions make their representing objects contractible'; 'Their study of coskeletal and truncated globular models also supplies context for the cutoffs' (Henry-Lanari).
test1.verdict: No equivalent found in searches A-K (abstract/snippet level only). Every ingredient has a named precedent; the coupling 'path object partial in the expansion index + contractibility from higher indices + top case from a coskeletal cutoff' was not found. Confidence limited by unread full texts (Lanari 2018, Taylor 2609.20860).

test2.evidence: The goal (i : X -> X+ is a weak equivalence for a J_n pushout) mentions no cylinder, path object, cutoff or induction order. L does contain 'path object => pushout lemma' (Henry 2016, Lanari 2020) and Lanari's full cylinders, so the generic path-object component is analytic relative to L; the partial (stationary below n), index-tailored objects and the descending order at fixed q are not subterms of the goal or of any L statement found. Syntactic size irrelevant: P_j for j<=n is trivial (D_j, D_{n+1}); the content is the choice.

test3.evidence: Paper: Secs 3-4 (all of the proof after the preliminaries) serve this scheme. Lean: cylinderPathData has dominated share 0.648 of the 856-declaration proof DAG, and cutoff_elementary_exactBoundaryTest (0.735) contains it. That is far above k = 20% of the whole DAG, and a fortiori of the mathematical core (~46% of the DAG once ~28% reflector/colimit plumbing and infrastructure are excluded). cylinder_oneSided_contractible alone is only 0.033: the bootstrap lemma is narrow, its consumers are wide.
test3.lean: family.json figures from a patched extractor (theorem foo.{v} bug); official 312_lean.json shows an empty DAG.

test4.pivot_distance: about 2 from L: from Lanari's stated obstruction (interpreting all operations needs contractible representing objects) and Henry's reduction, one must (a) give up the full path object for one tailored to a single expansion index n (stationary below n), and (b) see that its upper contractibility is exactly the higher-index cases, which requires (c) a cutoff q to start a descending induction. (c) is one step from Henry-Lanari's coskeletal models.
test4.chain_depth: 2 (needs the cutoff reflector C7 and whisker/tree contractibility C5 before the cylinders pay off)

final.justification: Eureka CANDIDATE only. No equivalent found (test 1, abstract-level searches); non-analytic in its partial/descending form (test 2) though the path-object strategy is in L; strongly load-bearing (test 3, 65% dominated share). F3: P_j are auxiliary objects built only for the proof; F2: the scheme turns the theorem's own higher-index cases into the input that makes them contractible. Kept at N3 rather than capped because the cap targets templated IH strengthenings, and here the new content is the auxiliary object whose contractibility the reversed induction supplies; the descending order alone (C3) is capped at N2. Fragile: falls to N2 if Lanari 2018's 'slightly less than a path object' or Taylor 2609.20860 is partial in the same sense, or if Test 4 shows easy rediscovery. Comparable in shape to Cook's device (cheap objects, P_j trivial below n, that cut an obstruction open since 2016/2018), but no downstream reuse is known yet; 317's stationary cylinders are an analogue, not a reuse of the bootstrap.

family_D.rests_on: C1 alone: the scheme 'index-n partial cylinders whose representing objects are contractible by the higher-index cases of a descending induction at a fixed coskeletal cutoff'. Every component graded separately (C2-C10) is N2 or below.
family_D.falls_to: D2 if (a) the full text of Taylor 2609.20860, Lanari 2018 (1809.07923, the 3-dimensional 'endofunctor that behaves like a path object', 'slightly less than a path object'), Henry-Lanari 2023 or Henry 2016 Sec 4 contains a path-like object partial in the expansion index with contractibility drawn from higher-dimensional cases; (b) Test 4 shows pre-cutoff models, given Lanari's stated obstruction and Henry's path-object reduction, propose 'only build the path object needed for index n and get its fillers from higher indices'; (c) an expert classifies it as the standard 'induction downward from a truncation' pattern already used in finite-dimensional (n-groupoid) cases; or (d) the scheme is judged a templated IH strengthening in substance (the cap), since its only role is to make the IH self-feeding.
family_D.not_transfer: Ingredients are transfer/N0 or variants: Lanari cylinders, homotopy rel boundary (stationary cylinders), coskeletal reflection (Henry-Lanari), contractible-coglobular interpretation (Ara, Bourke, Lumsdaine/van den Berg-Garner), small object argument, path-object retract argument (Quillen/Brown). D3 rests only on their coupling and order, so the cross-field exclusion does not apply; but the cross-field count is 1 and no new bridge exists.
family_D.correctness_caveat: Theorem 1.1 is Lean-backed and trusted as published (no IsCoherator instance is constructed, so non-vacuity is not formally shown; risk low). The homotopy hypothesis (title) is unformalized and rests on Henry 2016 plus a claimed typo fix in Henry's Lemma 5.3.11. Unreviewed; no expert reaction found.
family_D.speedup_note: The device is tailored to a single conjecture. Downstream reuse targets must be theorems other than Thm 1.1 and its corollaries (Cor 5.1/5.2, coherator independence, Taylor Thm 5.8 in the Ara-Henry convention are corollaries and do not count). Candidates: the pushout lemma for Grothendieck n-groupoids at finite n (Henry-Lanari; gives an internal-consistency check), coherators outside the arity-height convention (Maltsiniotis), Taylor's controlled theories / generalized pushout conjecture beyond the Ara-Henry convention, Grothendieck-Maltsiniotis (infinity,n)-categories, and family 317's strict Thomason setting (already solved without it - a negative control).
